output.brief: The August drop is almost entirely explained by the cooling failure on floors 6-8. Chiller CH-2 was down from 4 to 19 August. Rooms there ran 26-29 C. Floors 6-8 room-comfort scores fell from 8.4 to 6.1. Their overall score fell to 6.8 for checkouts during the outage and recovered to 8.4 once cooling was restored. Of the 74 negative comments, 56 were about heat, all from those floors. Floors 1-5 were essentially flat. Cleanliness scores, inspection pass rates and kiosk metrics did not move, and the survey method was unchanged. So there is no evidence against Orrin or the kiosks, and I would not serve notice or pull the kiosks. The rate rise may have added a little to the value-for-money dip on floors 1-5, but that dip is close to the usual August seasonal pattern, so the rate rise is unproven. I would not reverse it yet. Next steps: reinstate the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers, stock critical spares, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. Keep the August scores as they are, because excluding the outage month would hide a real failure. Guests already received an apology and a credit, so a return-stay offer is optional. I'm confident in this diagnosis. I haven't collected extra evidence, and more is unlikely to change these steps.
